comparison: Both evaluations strongly support claims C44-C50 regarding capsule impairing T6SS efficacy through reduced Hcp secretion. OpenEval provides detailed experimental validation (Figure 2A-D data), while peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as a core finding with 'compelling' evidence. High agreement with 87.5% claim overlap.

Both support the dual protective role of capsule (C31, C39-C41, C43). OpenEval validates with experimental data from Figure 1C-D showing differential survival against T6SS attacks. Peer reviewers affirm capsule 'protects against T6SS attacks' as an 'important' finding. Strong agreement on defensive mechanisms with 55.6% claim overlap.

Both support claims about capsule protection and serum resistance (C36-C38). OpenEval validates with Figure 1A-B experimental data on polysaccharide production and complement killing assays. Peer reviewers accept the protective role as part of the dual function finding. Partial overlap (33.3%) focusing on defensive aspects.

Both support claims C70-C73 regarding antibiotic-induced capsule overproduction and T6SS impairment. OpenEval notes experimental support from Figure 4A-C but acknowledges limitations and speculative environmental relevance. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as supporting evidence for the main finding. Agreement with 66.7% claim overlap.

Both support claims C59-C63 about bfmS mutant capsule overproduction reducing T6SS activity. OpenEval validates with Figure 3C-D data and genetic complementation controls. Peer reviewers accept capsule overproduction effects as part of the 'compelling' evidence for T6SS impairment. Agreement with 35.7% claim overlap.

Both support claims C64-C68 regarding capsule ultrastructure and T6SS inhibition correlation. OpenEval validates with TEM data (Figure 3E) but notes mechanistic link remains speculative. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the overall compelling evidence for capsule-mediated T6SS impairment. Agreement with 35.7% claim overlap.

Both support claims C56-C58 about bfmS mutant phenotypes. OpenEval validates with Figure 3A-B showing differential serum resistance and CPS profiles. Peer reviewers accept genetic modifications and their effects as part of the core findings. Agreement with 17.6% claim overlap.

Both support claims C78-C81 regarding T6SS assembly rates in capsule-overproducing strains. OpenEval validates with Figure 5A-B quantitative data but notes unexplained fluorescence decrease. Peer reviewers accept the mechanistic framework showing assembly is not limiting. Agreement with 36.4% claim overlap.

Both support claims C82-C85 comparing tslA and bfmS mutants to demonstrate assembly is not the limiting factor. OpenEval validates with Figure 5C-D experimental data. Peer reviewers accept this mechanistic conclusion as part of the compelling evidence. Strong agreement with 50% claim overlap.

Both support major conclusions C105-C107, C111 about dual protection mechanisms and T6SS regulation. OpenEval notes some mechanistic details (membrane tension, energy conservation) remain speculative. Peer reviewers describe overall evidence as 'compelling' and accept these interpretations. Agreement with 66.7% claim overlap.

Both support claims C86-C89 regarding growth phase-dependent Hcp degradation. OpenEval validates with Figure 6A-B data across multiple strains. Peer reviewers accept the Hcp degradation mechanism as part of the compelling overall findings. Agreement with 26.7% claim overlap.

Both support claims C90-C92 about post-transcriptional regulation of Hcp. OpenEval validates with Figure 6C-D time-course data but notes statistical analysis could be more robust. Peer reviewers accept this regulatory mechanism without specific concerns. Agreement with 20% claim overlap.

OpenEval rates claims C93-C94 as UNCERTAIN due to speculative polar effect interpretation, while peer reviewers accept the overall Hcp degradation findings as 'compelling' without raising specific concerns about this aspect. Divergence in confidence level with 13.3% claim overlap.

Both support claims C95-C96 regarding ClpXP-mediated Hcp degradation. OpenEval validates with Figure 7C data and Lon protease controls. Peer reviewers accept this regulatory mechanism as part of the overall findings. Agreement with 12.5% claim overlap.

Both support claim C103 about C-terminal recognition by ClpXP. OpenEval validates with Figure 7D experimental data on Hcp variants. Peer reviewers accept the degradation mechanism without specific concerns. Agreement with 5.9% claim overlap.

Both support claim C104 synthesizing post-transcriptional regulation findings. OpenEval considers this a reasonable synthesis of Figures 6-7 data. Peer reviewers accept the regulatory mechanism as part of compelling evidence. Agreement with 6.7% claim overlap.
